_note: The register of every edge type the medical multigraph may hold. It is a CONTRACT, not documentation: scripts/build_edges.py refuses any edge whose predicate is not registered here, whose subject or object vocabulary is not the one registered, or which has no source (rule zero, docs/weighted-graph-design.md). A new SNOMED CT-AU attribute in a later edition therefore fails the build until someone registers it on purpose. The snomed_attributes section is generated from the release by scripts/graph_register.py; everything else is authored.

_taxonomy._note: Every edge is a verb joining two nouns (concepts). `category` says what kind of meaning the edge carries, after the five-way frame worked out on 23 Sep 2026 -- nouns, verbs, adjectives, temporality, rationality -- extended with the kinds a cross-vocabulary graph needs. Signs and symptoms are NOUNS (SNOMED clinical findings), not adjectives; the adjective layer is the qualifier values that modify them.
_taxonomy.structure: is-a and part-of hierarchy between concepts of one vocabulary (the poly-hierarchy: 42% of standard SNOMED concepts have more than one parent)
_taxonomy.relation: a defining attribute joining two nouns: finding site, associated morphology, causative agent, due to, active ingredient
_taxonomy.action: the 'doing' verb: SNOMED procedure Method (excision, injection ...). LOINC's only verb axis, METHOD, is also action
_taxonomy.adjective: the object is a qualifier value: severity, laterality, interpretation (high/low/normal)
_taxonomy.temporality: occurrence, clinical course, episodicity, temporal context, LOINC TIME
_taxonomy.rationality: quantity: units, pack sizes, LOINC PROPERTY and SCALE. Numeric values themselves are NOT edges -- they live in typed tables (DRUG_STRENGTH, strength); only the unit or the kind of quantity is an edge
_taxonomy.identity: a cross-vocabulary equivalence or mapping: Maps to, exactMatch, xref. Never merges nodes -- the same substance in SNOMED and RxNorm stays two nodes and one identity edge
_taxonomy.commercial: listing and subsidy: PBS item, restriction
_taxonomy.evidence: a clinical assertion from a source: indication, contraindication, off-label use, disease-phenotype. Safety-relevant; defaults to corrected_pending_attestation where a person must sign off

_mechanisms: The five meanings are carried by three different mechanisms, and conflating them is what would sink an implementation: GRAPH EDGES (this register); TYPED TABLES for quantities (DRUG_STRENGTH's 2,966,568 rows, the compendium's strength table -- joins, never traversed); FREE-TEXT FIELDS in sources (PBS severity on 192 of 653 indications, episodicity on 42, 'Severe' and 'severe' distinct strings) which ride as edge attributes until bound.

vocabularies.SCT: SNOMED CT, keyed by SCTID. One vocabulary for international and AU-extension concepts (AMT included): SCTIDs are globally unique, so an AMT substance and the same SNOMED substance are ONE node
vocabularies.ICDO: ICD-O-3 (WHO International Classification of Diseases for Oncology), topography (C..) and morphology (..../.) codes. Named by code: the classification's labels are WHO's and are not loaded
vocabularies.ARTG: Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods entry, keyed by ARTG id (TGA)
vocabularies.RXE: OMOP RxNorm Extension, keyed by its OMOP concept_code
vocabularies.LOINC: LOINC terms (e.g. 2345-7), parts (LP...) and answers (LA...), keyed by code
vocabularies.ICD10CM: ICD-10-CM, keyed by code (used to score MONDO -> SNOMED independently)
vocabularies.PBS_INDICATION: PBS indication, keyed by indication_prescribing_txt_id; its name is the free-text condition
vocabularies.MONDO: MONDO disease, keyed by MONDO id
vocabularies.HP: Human Phenotype Ontology, keyed by HP id
vocabularies.CORPUS: a condition of this compendium's guideline corpus, keyed by its name
vocabularies.DC_TARGET: DrugCentral target, keyed by target_id: one protein, or a complex of several (a GABA-A receptor), as DrugCentral curates it
vocabularies.NCBIGENE: NCBI Gene, keyed by Entrez gene id (5743); the id HPO and DrugCentral both use
vocabularies.UCUM: A unit of measure, keyed by its UCUM code (mmol/L, g/L, 10*9/L); reached only by unit edges -- numbers are never nodes
vocabularies.UBERON: Uberon multi-species anatomy ontology, keyed by UBERON id
vocabularies.FMA: Foundational Model of Anatomy, keyed by FMA id (numeric part). Reached only as a cross-reference (RadLex, Uberon); FMA itself is not loaded
vocabularies.RADLEX: RadLex (RSNA radiology lexicon), keyed by RID. RSNA licence: read in place from RadLex.owl, never committed
vocabularies.RPID: RSNA Radiology Playbook orderable procedure, keyed by RPID
vocabularies.NCBITAXON: NCBI Taxonomy, keyed by taxon id (9606 = Homo sapiens)
vocabularies.MBS: Medicare Benefits Schedule item, keyed by item number (Department of Health, MBS XML)
vocabularies.MBS_GROUP: MBS group, keyed by category/group code (e.g. 5/I1)
vocabularies.MBS_CATEGORY: MBS category, keyed by number (1 professional attendances ... 6 pathology)
vocabularies.DOID: Human Disease Ontology, keyed by DOID number
vocabularies.NCIT: NCI Thesaurus, keyed by NCIt code (C...)
vocabularies.MESH: Medical Subject Headings (NLM), keyed by descriptor or supplementary record id (D..., C...) -- how PubMed indexes articles
vocabularies.ICD11: WHO ICD-11 foundation entity, keyed by foundation id
vocabularies.EFO: Experimental Factor Ontology, keyed by EFO number
vocabularies.UMLS: UMLS Metathesaurus concept, keyed by CUI (identifier only; UMLS content is not loaded)
vocabularies.MEDGEN: NCBI MedGen concept, keyed by MedGen UID
vocabularies.ICD10WHO: WHO ICD-10, keyed by code (codes only; WHO labels not loaded)
vocabularies.OMIMPS: OMIM phenotypic series, keyed by PS number
vocabularies.CHEBI: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest), keyed by ChEBI number
vocabularies.CHEMBL: ChEMBL compound, keyed by CHEMBL id
vocabularies.IUPHAR: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology ligand id
vocabularies.ICD11MMS: WHO ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, keyed by MMS code (e.g. LD24.61). Distinct from ICD11 (foundation ids, as MONDO cites them). Codes only
vocabularies.GARD: NIH Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center disease id
vocabularies.REACTOME: Reactome pathway, keyed by stable id (R-HSA-...)

predicates.label: likelihood ratio for the diagnosis when the finding is PRESENT (LR+; below 1 means presence lowers the odds)
subject: SCT
predicates.source: PubMed abstracts of diagnostic-accuracy reviews, transcribed to reference/diagnostic_accuracy.json (PMID per edge)
predicates.note: Values transcribed from the abstract's numbers only (the abstract itself is not stored), verified number by number against the cached abstract (scripts/verify_diagnostic_accuracy.py); attrs: lr, lr_ci (when published), sens / spec and their intervals, derived (LR computed from pooled sensitivity and specificity: no interval is invented), population, setting (calibrated_on), pmid. Finding and diagnosis bind to SNOMED CT-AU by exact term only. A clinical-safety edge: state corrected_pending_attestation until a person signs off. LRs may pool across Western primary care; priors never pool (prevalence_in). Where a source publishes only a RANGE of LRs across studies, the edge carries attrs.lr_range and no point estimate (method 'LR range across studies'): it may be displayed, never multiplied.

predicates.label: likelihood ratio for the diagnosis when the finding is ABSENT (LR-)

predicates.source: PubMed abstracts of diagnostic-accuracy reviews, transcribed to reference/diagnostic_accuracy.json (PMID per edge)
predicates.note: A separate edge: LR- is not 1/LR+. Same record, verification and attestation as finding_lr_if_present. Where a source publishes only a RANGE of LRs across studies, the edge carries attrs.lr_range and no point estimate (method 'LR range across studies'): it may be displayed, never multiplied.

predicates.note: The subject is the test (a SNOMED procedure, observable or result finding -- through the graph's loinc:is_a_snomed and loinc:sct_concept edges it reaches the LOINC codes that report it); attrs.result says which result (comparator, threshold, unit: 'BNP < 100 pg/mL'), attrs.lr / lr_ci, or attrs.lr_range where only a range across studies is published. Same transcription, verification, binding and attestation as finding_lr_if_present.

predicates.note: Kept apart from the diagnostic predicates: the object has not happened yet (death after cardiac arrest, severe alcohol withdrawal, a difficult intubation). attrs.when (present / absent), attrs.horizon where the source states one, attrs.lr / lr_range.

subject: SCT

Tier 3 recall is ordinal-only and lives in edge_authored as a look-up queue, never here -- SUPERSEDED 23 Sep 2026 by finding_lr_if_present / finding_lr_if_absent: a present finding can LOWER the odds (history of vaginal discharge, LR 0.3, for UTI), which 'suggests' / 'argues against' cannot say.

subject: SCT
predicates.note: For SNOMED ids arriving from foreign sources (DrugCentral's US conditions, Athena's LOINC targets in other extensions) that the Australian release does not carry. The same move item 17 made in the other direction. Only the nearest level is kept; ties keep all.

predicates.label: HPO phenotype shares a UMLS concept (CUI) with a SNOMED CT concept
subject: HP
predicates.source: UMLS Metathesaurus crosswalk HPO -> SNOMEDCT_US (UTS REST API, licensed; derived data not redistributed)
predicates.note: Signs and symptoms to SNOMED findings through a shared UMLS CUI. Only edges whose SNOMED name equals the HPO label load (hand check 40/40, Wilson lower bound 0.912 -> Tier 2), edge by edge. Differently named links were right 34/40 (85%, lower bound ~0.71 -> inadmissible) and wrong by narrowing (Polycythemia -> Polycythemia vera; Retinal hole -> Retinal round hole; Tardive dyskinesia -> Neuroleptic-induced tardive dyskinesia), so they are candidates for a person in cache/umls/hpo_snomed_candidates.tsv, not edges. Hierarchy preservation (64% on active Australian targets) is a diagnostic: it measures two ontologies' structures agreeing, not whether a mapping is right. Measured 23 Sep 2026.

predicates.label: HPO phenotype is cross-referenced by HPO to this concept
subject: HP
predicates.note: HPO's own xrefs; few, and not all exact (an xref can be a close match). MedDRA left out (MSSO licence).

predicates.label: LOINC term is represented by this SNOMED CT observable entity (LOINC Ontology)
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: SNOMED CT LOINC Extension 20260321, sct2_Identifier (LOINC num <-> SCTID, scheme 30051010000102)
predicates.note: The official, permanent binding of a LOINC number to its SCTID -- a lookup, not a mapping. Attrs carry the refset role (observation = result code, orderable), the 'Discouraged' annotation, and LOINC 2.83's CLASS / CLASSTYPE / STATUS. The observable is where SNOMED's Interprets points, which is what makes lab result -> finding a lookup chain.

predicates.label: LOINC orderable grouper (LABORDERS.ONTOLOGY) is represented by this SNOMED CT concept
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: SNOMED CT LOINC Extension 20260321, sct2_Identifier; class from LOINC 2.83
predicates.note: A separate predicate on purpose: the release notes say these groupers 'are not intended for and must not be used as result codes', so a traversal over results must not be able to reach them by accident.

predicates.label: a LOINC term's component, system or method part -- or, for a radiology term, its RadLex anatomy part -- maps to this SNOMED CT concept
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: LOINC 2.83 LoincPartLink_Primary (term -> part) joined to PartRelatedCodeMapping (part -> SNOMED CT); for radiology terms, LoincRsnaRadiologyPlaybook (term -> RadLex) joined to radlex:anatomy_sct
predicates.note: The one code-to-code route LOINC offers for its clinical and survey terms, which Athena and the LOINC Extension leave unbridged. attrs.part_type (COMPONENT: what is observed; SYSTEM: the body site or specimen; METHOD: the technique or modality), attrs.equivalence as LOINC states it (equivalent / narrower / wider -- a SYSTEM part 'Heart' maps narrower to both 'Heart structure' and 'Specimen from heart'). TIME, SCALE and PROPERTY parts, and the unspecified system 'XXX', are not loaded: they name an axis value, not a concept of the thing observed. Radiology terms have no SNOMED part map; their region-imaged and imaging-focus parts reach SNOMED through radlex:anatomy_sct instead, method 'RadLex anatomy: <route>', attrs.rid and attrs.route, and the tier of that route.

predicates.label: a LOINC term's analyte part (component, divisor, gene, challenge) is coded by LOINC to this concept
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: LOINC 2.83 LoincPartLink_Primary and LoincPartLink_Supplementary (DetailedModel links) joined to PartRelatedCodeMapping
predicates.note: What the test measures, in the analyte's own vocabulary. RxNorm and NCBI Gene are vocabularies the drug and gene sides already hold, so a drug-level test meets its drug and a genotype test its gene with no matching. attrs.link_type (Primary / DetailedModel), part_type, equivalence (equivalent / relatedto) as LOINC states it. Search links are not loaded.

predicates.label: LOINC mass-concentration term (US convention, mg/dL) and its substance-concentration counterpart (SI, mmol/L) -- the same measurement in the other unit
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: LOINC 2.83 axes (MCnc and SCnc, every other axis equal); molecular weight from PubChem by the component part's LOINC-asserted equivalent PubChem / ChEBI id
predicates.note: attrs.factor_mg_per_dL_to_mmol_per_L = 10 / MW, with the MW and its PubChem CID; null where the analyte has no equivalent chemical code (proteins, lipoprotein fractions) -- the pair is still an edge, the factor is not guessed. attrs.au_preferred (which of the two Australian laboratories report) comes from the RCPA SPIA Preferred Units Table and is null until it is loaded: Australian practice is not always molar (haemoglobin, albumin in g/L). scripts/unit_reconcile.py; reference/loinc_unit_counterparts.json.

predicates.label: Australian laboratories report this LOINC term in this unit (RCPA SPIA preferred unit)
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: RCPA SPIA Reporting Terminology Reference Sets (chemical pathology, haematology, immunopathology, microbiology serology, blood gases), NCTS release RCPA_v20260831 -- read in place, RCPA copyright
predicates.note: attrs: the RCPA display unit, LOINC's example (US-convention) UCUM unit for the same code, and factor_us_example_to_au where the two differ only in scale (haemoglobin g/dL -> g/L, x10); null where they differ in kind. Which of a mass / molar pair Australia reports is read off these edges (loinc:unit_counterpart attrs.au_preferred is filled from them at build time). The graph built from this is not for redistribution, as the RCPA content it carries is licensed.

predicates.label: a result of this LOINC term, with the interpretation in attrs, is what SNOMED CT's definition of this finding interprets
subject: LOINC
predicates.source: SNOMED CT-AU 20260731 Interprets (363714003) + Has interpretation (363713009), reached two ways -- PARALLEL edges, told apart by method: the SNOMED CT LOINC Extension 20260321 observable on Component and specimen; and OMOP Athena v5.0 29-AUG-26's placement of the LOINC term under the interpreted procedure, restricted by the LOINC Extension's specimen
predicates.note: Lab result -> finding. SNOMED's is-a does NOT close this chain: lab findings interpret measurement PROCEDURES ('Random blood sugar low' interprets 'Random blood glucose measurement'), and the LOINC Ontology places LOINC terms under OBSERVABLES, so subsumption reaches 14 findings. The bridge is the analyte: the LOINC observable and the Interprets target share a Component and a compatible specimen. Each route (the edge's method) earns its own tier from reference/interprets_handcheck.json: the analyte join 79/80; Athena with the target's specimen 39/40; Athena with a specimen-less target and a blood-family LOINC specimen 40/40 (an assumption that route supplies, so it is scored alone). Unrestricted, Athena's new edges were right 27 times in 53, and are not built; attrs carry the interpretation, the Interprets target, the component and both specimens. Definitional, not diagnostic: DKA is defined partly by a raised glucose, not diagnosed by one.

not_imported.drug_drug (DrugBank): PrimeKG's drug-drug layer is from DrugBank, whose open data is non-commercial. Not imported.
not_imported.drug_effect (SIDER): PrimeKG's side-effect layer is from SIDER, non-commercial. Not imported.
not_imported.omics layers: protein, gene, pathway, GO and anatomy-expression layers are outside the compendium's scope.
not_imported.PrimeKG's grouped diseases: PrimeKG collapsed 22,205 MONDO concepts into 17,080 by embedding similarity -- a union of concepts, the upper approximation that scored worst in the pregnancy work. MONDO is used at its own granularity instead.
